ASSISTANCE TO JAPANESE GENDARMERIE

At 3.20 p.m. on the 28-2-38 J.D.C. 182 K. Sugimoto
attached to Bubbling Well Station, came to this Station ac-
companied by Sergeant Ohyama of the Western Branch of
the Japanese Gendarmerie situated at No. 94 Jessfield
Road. It appears that the latter named proceeded to
Bubbling Well Station for assistance to visit premises
situated at House No. 3, Lane 106 Medhurst Road, but on
it being ascertained that the address in question was
situated in the Chengtu Road district, the authorities
concerned were directed to this Station by J.D.C. 182.
Questioned as to the purpose and object of the visit to
the premises in question, Segt. Ohyama stated that the
Japanese military authorities had received information
that the premises referred to was the residence of General
Chen Nyi (陳儀), Governor of the Fukien Province, the
Japanese authorities desired to visit the premises and
ascertain if their information was correct or otherwise,
they did not desire to search or seal any properties con-
nected with the premises. Instructions to proceed and ren-
der the assistance desired was given by the D.C. (Crime)
through the D.D.O."A" after the object of the visit of the
representative of the Japanese Gendarmerie had been ex-
plained. Assistance was rendered by the undersigned an

协助日本宪兵队

1938年2月28日下午3时20分，隶属于静安寺捕房的日本宪兵队第182号人员 K. Sugimoto（杉本），在日本宪兵队西区分队（位于极司菲尔路94号）的大山（Ohyama，音译）军曹陪同下，来到本捕房。据悉，后者前往静安寺捕房寻求协助，以便视察位于麦赫斯特路106弄3号的处所，但在查明该地址属于成都路辖区后，经日本宪兵队第182号人员指示，有关当局被指引至本捕房。当被问及视察上述处所的目的和意图时，大山军曹称，日本军方当局收到情报，称所述处所为福建省主席陈仪（Chen Nyi）将军的寓所，日本当局希望视察该处所并核实其情报是否属实，他们并不希望对与该处所相关的任何财产进行搜查或查封。在日本宪兵队代表说明了此次访问的目的后，经由“A”区副总监通过犯罪科总监下达了指令，要求前往并提供所需的协助。由下述人员及

D.S.I. Tsai Liu, it was learned that General Chen Nyi had
removed from the aforementioned premises sometime during
the month of August, 1937, the present occupant being one
Yang Kyien Chow, age 23, native of Ningpo, a partner of the
"Bau Dah" (保大) Jin Sen Co., 503 Avenue Edward VII. The
present tenant stated that he had occupied the premises
on or about the 10-10-37, he stated that the premises
were vacant and devoid of furniture, fittings etc; and that
the present contents of the premises were his own property.
Yang Kyien Chow (楊建同) stated that the house was the pro-
perty of Mr. Tsha Kyu Sing (蔡九星), residing at House 1,
Lane 84 Medhurst Road. One named Wong Mueu Foh (王茂福),
representative of Mr. Tsha Kyu Sing was interviewed and
in the presence of the representatives of the Japanese
Gendarmerie verified the statement of the tenant regarding
the ownership of the property in question and the statement o
of Yang regarding the ownership of furniture and date of
occupancy by the latter. The representative of the Japanese
Gendarmerie appeared satisfied that no properties belonging
to General Chen Nyi, were housed on the premises, they then
departed after expressing their appreciation for the as-
sistance rendered.

特别科督察蔡刘（Tsai Liu，音译）得知，陈仪将军已于1937年8月间的某个时候搬离上述处所，目前的居住者为杨建同（Yang Kyien Chow），23岁，宁波人，系爱多亚路503号“保大”金森公司合伙人。现任租户称，他于1937年10月10日左右入住该处所，并称该处所当时空置且无家具、装置等物品；目前处所内的物品均为其个人财产。杨建同（楊建同）称，该房屋产权属于居住在麦赫斯特路84弄1号的蔡九星（Tsha Kyu Sing，音译）先生。一位名为王茂福（Wong Mueu Foh，音译）的人，作为蔡九星先生的代表接受了问询，并在日本宪兵队代表在场的情况下，证实了租户关于所述房产所有权的陈述，以及杨建同关于家具所有权及其入住日期的陈述。日本宪兵队代表似乎确信该处所内没有属于陈仪将军的任何财产，随后在表达了对所提供协助的感谢后离去。

ASSISTANCE TO JAPANESE MILITARY POLICE.

At 6.45p.m. 26.2.38 the Japanese Consular Police informed the station that a party of Japanese Military Police would come ~~t~~o assistance to visit an address in Hwakee Avenue, Bubbling Well Road.

At 7.05p.m. 26.2.38 Sgt.Maj.Shimowatari i/c of a party of J.M.P. came to the station and requested assistance to visit No.121 Hwakee Avenue, Room No.8, to arrest a male Chinese Lee Zau Ping(李社平) alias Tsu(朱) who was said to be i/c of the Shanghai Intelli_gence Bureau of the Military Committee of China.

（印：MUNICIPAL POLICE / 28 FEB. 1938 / SPECIAL BRANCH）

Assistance was given by S.I.Fowler, D.C.Sugimoto, C.D.S. 176 and the undersigned. No person was found at the stated address under the names given, but the room had been rented by a male student formerly of Chinese University named Zung Wen Sung(張忠士).

At thr request of the J.M.P. the contents of a writing desk was searched but nothing bearing out the allegations of the Japanese party was found.

After withdrawing from the above address, Sgt. Maj. Shimowatari stated that he did not wish further action to be taken until he had made further enquiries.

1938年2月26日。

南汇报告 78/38。

协助日本军事警察。

1938年2月26日下午6时45分，日本领事警察通知本站，一队日本军事警察将前来寻求协助，以视察静安寺路华克路（Hwakee Avenue，音译）的一处地址。

1938年2月26日下午7时05分，日本军事警察小队负责人岛渡（Shimowatari，音译）警长来到本站，请求协助视察华克路121号8室，以逮捕一名中国男子李社平（Lee Zau Ping），别名朱（Tsu），据称他是中国军事委员会上海情报局负责人。

（印章：工部局警务处 / 1938年2月28日 / 特别科）

协助工作由特别科督察 Fowler、侦探 Sugimoto、华人侦探社第176号人员及下述人员提供。在指定地址未找到使用上述姓名的人员，但该房间已由一名前中国大学的学生张忠士（Zung Wen Sung，音译）租用。

应日本军事警察的要求，对一张写字台的内容进行了搜查，但未发现任何能佐证日本方面指控的物品。

从上述地址撤离后，岛渡警长表示，在他进行进一步调查之前，不希望采取进一步行动。

The J.P.C. and a Japanese in civilian clothes accompanied

The J.P.C. and the Japanese in civilian clothes questioned

The Japanese in civilian clothes is alleged to have searched
all the drawers in the room. Nothing of an incriminating nature
was found, nor was any property taken away.

Tsung Tsang Sz, S Waung Sz and S Ah Noen were taken to
Room 346 at the Grand Hotel by the J.P.C. and the Japanese
civilian where Tsung Tsang Sz was subjected to further interroga-
tion. She was accused of being the wife of Ngan Tsung Hwa
(颜振华), the person who engaged Room 336, where the pamphlet
was found. It was not until she produced letters from Wenchow
addressed to her husband that they believed her story.

At this juncture, 8.15 p.m., Zung Au Ching who is a paper
broker by trade and also a native of Wenchow visited Room 346 to
see Tsung Wo Sung. He was detained and questioned and later
brought to the station with the females.

Since these four persons have been detained at Louisa Station
the Japanese Military Authorities have made no further requests
to interview them.

该日本警察和一名便衣日本人陪同 S. Ah Noen（施阿囡，音译）前往汕头路18号，他们进入了一间由 Tsung Tsang Sz（宗藏氏，音译）和 S Waung Sz（施王氏，音译）居住的后楼房间。

该日本警察和便衣日本人询问 Tsung Tsang Sz 是谁预订了大华饭店的346号房间，她回答说是她的丈夫。

据称，那名便衣日本人搜查了房间里所有的抽屉。未发现任何具有定罪性质的物品，也未带走任何财产。

Tsung Tsang Sz、S Waung Sz 和 S Ah Noen 被该日本警察和便衣日本人带到大华饭店的346号房间，在那里 Tsung Tsang Sz 受到了进一步的审讯。她被指控是颜振华（Ngan Tsung Hwa）的妻子，颜振华是预订336号房间的人，传单就是在那里发现的。直到她出示了从温州寄给她丈夫的信件后，他们才相信了她的说法。

此时，即晚上8点15分，职业为纸张经纪人且同为温州人的 Zung Au Ching（宗奥清，音译）来到346号房间看望 Zung Wo Sung（宗武松，音译）。他被扣留并受到讯问，随后与几名女性一起被带到捕房。

自这四人在路易莎捕房（Louisa Station，即老闸捕房）被拘留以来，日本军事当局未再提出审讯他们的要求。

1938年5月5日晚上8点45分，“A”区总监 H. Robertson 先生发布了

pages.en:
Zung Tsang Sz
Wenchow, Chekiang. C.D.S. 47 Laung Kying Daung.
Louza Station 5-5-38

My name is Zung Tsang Sz, aged 31 years, native of Wenchow
Chekiang, at present residing in Room No. 346 of the Grand
Hotel. My husband is called Zung Woo Sung and he is a paper
dealer. We live together in the said room. As my husband
came to Shanghai to do paper business, he brought me with him
so that I could enjoy something new to me. At 4 p.m. on the
4-5-38, my sister, who is now residing at No. 18 Swatow Road,
invited me to dine with her. I accepted the invitation and
at 5 p.m. whilst I was at her home, my brother-in-law's concu-
bine, named Sz Wong Sz, sent my niece Sz Ah Noen to Room No. 34
of the Grand Hotel to call my husband Zung Woo Sung to come to
her home to dine with us. About 20 minutes later, my husband
failed to come and we saw that two Japanese came together with
Sz Ah Noen. They entered the upstairs back room where we
were sitting and talking. One of the Japanese was in full
police uniform, whilst the other in a suit of cream coloured
foreign clothing. On being questioned as to who was living
in room 346 of the Grand Hotel, I replied I was the person
residing therein. At this juncture, the Japanese in civilian
dress made a search of all the drawers in the said room, but
nothing was found by him. They then brought Sz Wong Sz, Sz
Ah Noen and myself to room No. 346 of the Grand Hotel. They
said that I was the wife of one named Ngan, to which I firmly
and said I
denied that did not know anyone by this name, but the Japanese
would not believe me. So I produced all the letters addressed
to my husband which we had received from our shop in Wenchow.
Later we were brought to the Police Station by the foreign and
Chinese detectives. The above is my true statement.
pages.zh:
宗藏氏（Zung Tsang Sz）
浙江温州。华人侦探社 47 梁庆堂（Laung Kying Daung，音译）。
老闸捕房 1938年5月5日

我叫宗藏氏，31岁，浙江温州人，现居住在大华饭店346号房间。我丈夫叫宗武松（Zung Woo Sung，音译），是一名纸商。我们共同居住在该房间。因为我丈夫来上海做纸张生意，他带我一起来，让我见识新鲜事物。1938年5月4日下午4点，现居住在汕头路18号的我的妹妹邀请我去她家吃饭。我接受了邀请，下午5点当我在她家时，我妹夫的小妾，名叫施王氏（Sz Wong Sz，音译），派我的侄女施阿囡（Sz Ah Noen，音译）去大华饭店34号房间叫我丈夫宗武松来她家与我们一起吃饭。大约20分钟后，我丈夫没来，我们看到两名日本人与施阿囡一起来到。他们进入了我们就坐交谈的后楼房间。其中一名日本人穿着全套警服，另一名穿着米色西式服装。当被问及谁住在大华饭店346号房间时，我回答我就是住在那里的人。此时，那名便衣日本人搜查了该房间的所有抽屉，但他什么也没找到。随后他们将施王氏、施阿囡和我带到大华饭店346号房间。他们说我是某位姓颜的人的妻子，我坚决否认，并表示我不认识这个名字的人，但日本人不相信我。于是我拿出了我们从温州店铺收到的所有寄给我丈夫的信件。后来我们被外籍和华人侦探带到捕房。以上是我的真实陈述。

pages.en:
Sz Ah Noen.
Taichow, Chekiang. C.D.S. 47 Laung Aying Daug.
Louza Station 5-5-38

My name is Sz Ah Noen, aged 13 years, native of Taichow,
Chekiang, residing at No. 18 Swatow Road. My father is called
Sz Si Yuen and he is a tea-leaf dealer.

At about 3 p.m. on the 4-5-38, on the instructions of
my step mother Sz Wong Sz, I proceeded to room No. 346 of the Grand
Hotel to call one Zung Woo Sung to come to my home to take
dinner. On entering the room I found that Zung Woo Sung was
not in. I then came out of the room and proceeded to Room
No. 336 to have a look. Whilst I was about to push open the
door of the latter mentioned room, I was suddenly caught hold
of by a Japanese policeman (in full uniform), who asked me whom
I was looking for. I replied that I was coming to look for
Zung Woo Sung of room No. 346. He further asked me where I
was from and I replied, from No. 18 Swatow Road. The Japanese
policeman then asked me to accompany him to my home. On arrival
the Japanese policeman immediately followed me upstairs and at
this time my step mother Sz Wong Sz and Zung Tsang Sz were in
the back upstairs room. The Japanese policeman and one other
Japanese who was in civilian dress then questioned my step
mother and Zung Tsang Sz. I also saw that the Japanese in
civilian dress made a search of all the drawers in the said
room. They later brought three of us, my step mother, Zung
Tsang Sz and myself, to Room 346 of the Grand Hotel, where they
later handed us over to the foreign and Chinese detectives, who
then escorted us to the Police Station.

This is my true statement.

Cross-marked, Sz Ah Noen.
pages.zh:
施阿囡（Sz Ah Noen）。
浙江台州。华人侦探社 47 梁爱英道（Laung Aying Daug，音译）。
老闸捕房 1938年5月5日

我叫施阿囡，13岁，浙江台州人，居住在汕头路18号。我父亲叫施思源（Sz Si Yuen，音译），是一名茶叶经销商。

1938年5月4日下午3点左右，遵照继母施王氏的指示，我前往大华饭店346号房间，叫宗武松来我家吃晚饭。进入房间后，我发现宗武松不在。于是我走出房间，去336号房间看看。正当我要推开后一个房间的门时，我突然被一名日本警察（身穿全套制服）抓住，他问我在找谁。我回答说我来找346号房间的宗武松。他又问我从哪里来，我回答从汕头路18号来。然后日本警察让我陪他去我家。到达后，日本警察立即跟随我上楼，当时我的继母施王氏和宗藏氏在后楼房间里。那名日本警察和另一名便衣日本人随后讯问了我的继母和宗藏氏。我还看到那名便衣日本人搜查了该房间的所有抽屉。后来他们把我们三人，即我的继母、宗藏氏和我，带到大华饭店346号房间，随后我们将移交给外籍和华人侦探，由他们护送我们去捕房。

这是我的真实陈述。

施阿囡画押。

pages.en:
Zung Hao Ching
Wenchow                                //      S.D.S. 47
Louza Stn.          5-5-38

My name is Zung Hao Ching, age 31, native of Wenchow,
Chekiang, residing at No. 3 Tuh Ying Li alleyway off Rue Petit,
F.C.  I am a paper dealer and grocer and run the business under
the name of Dong Shing Foh Hong.

At about 8.30 p.m. 4-5-38 I went to the Grand Hotel to
visit my friend named Zung Foo Sung who had opened a room No.346.
He is a fellow countryman of mine, and I visited him because
he is a stranger in Shanghai.  When I was arriving outside
of the room, I saw a number of policemen and detectives inside.
Being ignorant of what had happened, I entered the room and
was put under arrest by the police who later brought me to the
station.

The above is my true statement.

Sgd. Zung Hao Ching.
pages.zh:
宗浩清（Zung Hao Ching）
温州                                //      S.D.S. 47
老闸捕房          1938年5月5日

我叫宗浩清，31岁，浙江温州人，居住在法租界贝勒路（Rue Petit）屠营里（Tuh Ying Li，音译）3号。我是一名纸商和杂货商，以“东盛发号”（Dong Shing Foh Hong，音译）的名义经营业务。

1938年5月4日晚上8点30分左右，我去大华饭店拜访我的朋友宗福松（Zung Foo Sung，音译），他开了346号房间。他是我的同乡，我拜访他是因为他在上海人生地不熟。当我到达房间外时，我看到里面有许多警察和侦探。由于不知道发生了什么事，我走进房间并被警察逮捕，随后被带到捕房。

以上是我的真实陈述。

签名：宗浩清。

pages.en:
Sze Saung Sz
Taichong                                O.J.P. 47
Louisa Str.             5-5-38

My name is Sze Saung Sz, age 36, native of Taichong,
residing at No. 18 Newton Road. My husband Sze Si-Tseng is
a tea dealer. I have resided at the above for over three
years. Sung Woo Sung is my relative, his wife Sung Tsang Sz
being the younger sister of my husband's first wife. He
opened a room No. 346 in the Grand Hotel.

At 4.00 p.m. 4-5-38 Sung Tsang Sz came to my home for
recreation and remained with me to take supper. I sent my
daughter named Sze Ah Hoon to go to Room 346 of the Grand Hotel
to call Sung Woo Sung to come to my home for supper. After about
20 minutes my daughter returned together with two Japanese one
of whom was dressed in police uniform and the other in cream
coloured foreign clothes. Whilst in my room (situated above
the kitchen), the two Japanese asked me who opened room
No. 346 in the Grand Hotel. I replied that it was booked by
the husband of Sung Tsang Sz who was then present in my room.
The Japanese in plain clothes then searched all drawers in my
room but nothing of an incriminating nature was found by him.
They then brought me together with Sung Tsang Sz and my daughter
to room No. 346 of the Grand Hotel from where we were later
escorted to the police station by both foreign and Chinese
detectives.

The above is my true statement.

Cross-marked by
Sze Yang Sz
pages.zh:
施松氏（Sze Saung Sz）
太仓                                O.J.P. 47
路易莎街（老闸捕房）             1938年5月5日

我叫施松氏，36岁，太仓人，居住在牛顿路18号。我丈夫施思曾（Sze Si-Tseng，音译）是一名茶商。我在上述地址已居住三年多。宋武松（Sung Woo Sung，音译）是我的亲戚，他的妻子宋藏氏（Sung Tsang Sz，音译）是我丈夫原配的妹妹。他在大华饭店开了346号房间。

1938年5月4日下午4点，宋藏氏来我家消遣，并留下来与我共进晚餐。我派我的女儿施阿芬（Sze Ah Hoon，音译）去大华饭店346号房间叫宋武松来我家吃晚饭。大约20分钟后，我女儿和两名日本人一起回来，其中一人穿着警服，另一人穿着米色西式服装。在我的房间里（位于厨房楼上），两名日本人问我在大华饭店是谁开了346号房间。我回答说是当时在我房间里的宋藏氏的丈夫预订的。那名便衣日本人随后搜查了我房间里的所有抽屉，但他未发现任何具有定罪性质的物品。随后他们将我和宋藏氏及我的女儿带到大华饭店346号房间，之后我们由外籍和华人侦探护送至捕房。

以上是我的真实陈述。

施杨氏（Sze Yang Sz）画押
